p: Edinburgh's an easy city to get excited in, and that energy carries right into an escape room. A few pointers for a smooth game: listen properly to the briefing, as hosts often explain how certain locks or mechanisms work. Keep found items together so they don't get lost under coats. And if one person has been stuck on the same puzzle for ages, rotate them out. You'll be amazed how often the answer jumps out at someone who's only just looked.

Visiting groups find it a brilliant ice-breaker. If you're in town for a hen or stag weekend, a work trip or a family get-together, an hour of puzzling is a cracking way to get everyone talking before the main event.

Getting there is simple. Waverley station is a short walk away, and the trams now run all the way down Leith Walk to Leith and Newhaven, which makes it easy to hop between the city centre and the shore. Once you're out, the Royal Mile and the Old Town are within easy reach for a wander through the closes and wynds, while the Scottish National Portrait Gallery on Queen Street, with its glorious red sandstone building, is close by too. For a bigger leg-stretch, Holyrood Park and Arthur's Seat offer a proper hill climb right in the middle of the city. Dynamic Earth, near the Scottish Parliament, is a great family pick if you've still got energy to burn, and Leith's waterfront is stacked with restaurants for an evening out.
